claims.statement: The reviewer and analyzer are two separate deep-agent graphs registered in langgraph.json as `reviewer` (agent.graphs.reviewer:traced_reviewer_agent) and `analyzer` (agent.graphs.analyzer:traced_analyzer).

get_reviewer_agent builds the reviewer deep agent per run with a reviewer-only toolset (fetch_review_diff, add_finding, update_finding, list_findings, publish_review, resolve_finding_thread, reply_to_finding_thread plus read helpers), returning an empty agent when there is no thread_id or the graph is not loaded for execution.
get_reviewer_agent copies the incoming config before mutating it so it does not clobber the caller's recursion_limit.

PrepareReviewerRunMiddleware performs deterministic non-LLM setup before the first model call: it ensures the sandbox, mints and caches a repo-scoped GitHub App installation token as a bot token, and clones-or-fetches plus force-checks-out the PR head via prepare_review_repo.

The reviewer computes a unified diff and the set of in-diff (file, line) tuples during run prep and passes both as diff_text and diff_line_set in run state so add_finding can validate at creation time rather than at GitHub-publish time.
Findings persist in LangGraph thread metadata under the canonical reviewer thread so they survive sandbox eviction and are queryable cross-thread by filtering metadata.kind == reviewer.

The Finding TypedDict records severity, confidence, category, title, file plus start/end line and side, in_diff, description, optional suggestion, status, first_seen/last_confirmed SHAs, GitHub comment/thread/resolved-thread id lists, surface_state, human-reply bookkeeping, diff_hunk, a content fingerprint, and an interactions log.

add_finding rejects any finding whose start_line..end_line range is not part of the PR diff, returning success:false with in_diff:false so the model does not re-anchor or retry; out-of-diff findings are disabled.
add_finding resolves diff context from run state first, then configurable, then a fresh fetch_pr_diff, and stores an extracted diff_hunk on the finding when diff text is available.

publish_review batches findings above the severity threshold (default medium, status open, capped at REVIEW_FINDING_CAP) into one GitHub PR Review with a fixed host-formatted summary line and one inline comment per surfaced finding, appending a fenced suggestion block when present.
Each published inline comment embeds an open-swe-review-comment JSON marker so later runs can re-locate the finding's GitHub thread by finding id.

After posting, publish_review stores GitHub comment/thread ids back on each finding, resolves GitHub threads for findings moved to resolved via the GraphQL resolveReviewThread mutation, and advances the reviewer thread's last_reviewed_sha to the reviewed head.

reconcile_findings_with_review_threads syncs tracked findings against current GitHub review-thread state before each run: it records new comment/thread ids and marks findings surfaced, folds a finding to resolved when all its threads are resolved or outdated, and captures the latest human reply as a needs_reassessment interaction with a reconciliation note.

The reviewer opts into allow_replacement=True for its sandbox because the sandbox holds only a checkout re-derived each run and the durable findings live on the thread, so an unreachable sandbox is replaced rather than bricking reviews on that PR; only when replacement also fails does the run die with a typed on-PR notification.

The analyzer graph learns a per-repo review-style prompt for the reviewer by mining historical human PR review feedback and the reviewer's own past finding outcomes, reusing the sandbox and gh pattern with a user OAuth or App token wired into the sandbox proxy.

The analyzer_mode in configurable selects bootstrap vs continual mode; bootstrap crawls historical merged-PR feedback for a cold-start repo while continual reads reviewer finding outcomes via read_finding_outcomes to refine an existing prompt, each mapped to a bundled SKILL.md playbook that is authoritative for the procedure.

The two analyzer SKILL.md playbooks are served to the deepagents SkillsMiddleware as virtual files via a StateBackend mounted at the /skills/ route in a CompositeBackend, seeded into the run input files channel by build_skill_files, so nothing is written to the execution sandbox.

The analyzer's save_review_style_prompt tool persists the synthesized custom_prompt (plus summary, reviewers, and counts) to the REVIEW_STYLES store keyed by review_style_full_name and marks the record completed.

On a successful save_review_style_prompt, ensure_continual_cron idempotently registers one daily LangGraph continual-learning cron per repo, staggered by a hash of the repo name across 05:00-08:59 UTC.

The nightly continual cron is threadless but its configurable pins the repo's deterministic review_style_thread_id, because otherwise get_analyzer would early-return an empty agent and no-op; the threadless run carries no message history so runs do not accumulate across nights, and it authenticates via a GitHub App installation token resolved inside get_analyzer.
Reviewer preparation loads repository-provided skills only from the PR base SHA into a directory outside the checkout, so a PR-head change cannot inject a SKILL.md instruction into the reviewer.

GitHub PR review dispatch derives the deterministic reviewer thread, records PR metadata and a head SHA, and dispatches the `reviewer` assistant; ready-for-review skips work when that head already equals the persisted last_reviewed_sha.
